issues.legal_issue: A possession claim may be decreed where ownership has already been finally determined in the claimant’s favour in earlier litigation.
material_facts: The claimant brought a suit for possession of part of a property occupied by the opposing party, who disputed the claimant’s ownership.
In an earlier partition suit brought by the opposing party, the claim that the property was jointly owned had been rejected, and that determination was affirmed on appeal.
The claimant’s title documents and land records also stood in her favour.
issues.conclusion: The possession claim was properly decreed because the ownership issue had already been decided in the claimant’s favour and did not need to be decided again.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure gives finality to issues already decided between the parties. The prior determination of ownership therefore barred relitigation of that issue, and the possession claim could be decreed on that basis.

predicates.possession_and_damages_proceeding: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking possession from an occupant and also sought damages.
predicates.prior_final_ownership_determination_for_: An earlier final determination between the parties resolved ownership in favour of the claimant.
predicates.occupant_in_possession: The opposing party occupied the property for which the claimant sought possession.

issues.definition: When a possession-and-damages proceeding concerns property occupied by the opposing party and ownership has already been finally determined for the claimant, the possession claim may be decreed.

issues.legal_issue: A damages claim that remains undecided cannot be decreed solely on the basis that ownership has been determined in the claimant’s favour.
material_facts: The claimant sought both possession and damages for the opposing party’s occupation.
The earlier litigation had decided ownership but had not decided the claimant’s entitlement to damages or their amount.
The damages claim had not otherwise been decided in the current suit when the High Court decreed the entire suit.
issues.conclusion: The High Court ought not to have decreed the damages claim merely on the basis of the earlier ownership determination; the unresolved damages question required separate consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Order XII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a court, in its discretion, to give judgment on admissions of fact at any stage, including admissions made otherwise than in pleadings. It does not justify deciding a separate, unresolved claim merely because another issue is admitted or has already been determined. Karam Kapahi v. Lal Chand Public Charitable Trust, Charanjit Lal Mehra v. Kamal Saroj Mahajan, and Uttam Singh Duggal & Co. Ltd. v. United Bank of India support the breadth and discretionary character of the rule and its purpose of enabling speedy judgment on matters not in controversy.

predicates.possession_and_damages_proceeding: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking possession from an occupant and also sought damages.
predicates.damages_claim_unresolved: The claimant’s entitlement to damages or the amount of damages has not been decided in the earlier litigation or the current proceeding.
predicates.ownership_only_issue_previously_decided: The earlier litigation determined ownership but did not determine the damages claim.

issues.definition: If a possession-and-damages proceeding includes a damages claim that remains undecided and only ownership was previously determined, the damages claim cannot be decreed on the ownership determination alone.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may resolve an undecided damages claim without remand where the circumstances make remand unnecessary and a sum already deposited is just and proper compensation.
material_facts: The damages claim had not been decided in the earlier suit or the current suit.
During the appeal, the occupant deposited a sum in the claimant’s account in compliance with the Supreme Court’s direction.
The parties were mother and son, and the occupant had used the property without authorization.
issues.conclusion: The Court considered the deposited sum just and proper for the damages claim and declined to remand the matter for determination of the amount.
issues.legal_principle: Order XII Rule 6 is discretionary and permits judgment on admissions, but unresolved questions ordinarily remain for adjudication. In this case, considering the deposit, the parties’ relationship, and the unauthorized occupation, the Court resolved the damages claim itself rather than remanding it.

rule.if: appeal_in_possession_and_damages_case and damages_amount_unresolved and court_directed_deposit_made and close_family_relationship and unauthorized_occupation

predicates.appeal_in_possession_and_damages_case: An appeal concerns a proceeding seeking possession and damages for occupation of property.
predicates.damages_amount_unresolved: The amount payable as damages has not previously been determined.
predicates.court_directed_deposit_made: The occupant made a deposit in compliance with a direction of the appellate court.
predicates.close_family_relationship: The claimant and occupant had a close family relationship.
predicates.unauthorized_occupation: The occupant used the property without authorization.

issues.definition: Where an appeal concerns an unresolved damages amount, a court-directed deposit has been made, the parties have a close family relationship, and the occupation was unauthorized, the appellate court may resolve the damages claim without remanding it.

issues.legal_issue: An occupant may be permitted to remain temporarily in possession subject to payment for use and occupation and surrender of the property by the specified deadline.
material_facts: The Court affirmed the decree for possession in favour of the claimant.
The occupant was the claimant’s son and was permitted to remain in the property temporarily.
The Court required monthly payment for use and occupation and provided for execution of the possession and damages decree if the occupant failed to vacate or pay as directed.
issues.conclusion: The occupant was permitted to remain temporarily in possession on payment of monthly damages, but the claimant could execute the decree for possession and damages if the occupant failed to vacate and hand over possession or failed to make the required payments by the deadline.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its discretion in disposing of the appeal by allowing temporary continued occupation on payment for use and occupation, while preserving execution of the decree in the event of non-compliance.

predicates.appeal_against_possession_decree: An appeal concerns a decree requiring an occupant to give possession of property to the claimant.
predicates.occupant_allowed_temporary_continued_pos: The court permits the occupant to remain in the property temporarily after deciding the possession claim.
predicates.payment_for_use_and_occupation_required: The court requires payment for use and occupation during the permitted temporary possession.

issues.definition: When an occupant is permitted to remain temporarily after an appeal concerning a possession decree, continued possession depends on making the required payments and surrendering the property as directed.
